title: Rowing
text: Any student-athlete can tell you the amount of time, energy, and dedication it takes to be part of a team and also a full-time student. Rowing includes many early mornings and tests to your physical and mental strength. However, it also nurtures ambition, grit, passion, power, and a strong value of teamwork. No win can happen without every single person in a boat.

title: Rowing
text:
UCSB Rowing
Under the guidance of Coach Brooke Downes, I rowed with some amazing women for my two years on the team. My time here included a rigorous 6-day practice schedule but paid off with many medals and awards! This team is truly special and contains some very powerful women with multifaceted talents and interests. Each member is not just high-achieving in their sport, but also in academics, community engagement, and extracurriculars.

title: Rowing
text:
Berkeley High Crew
Berkeley High Crew introduced me to rowing when I needed it most. Rowing showed me the sheer strength of ones mind and that the human body, and ones-self, is more capable than anyone realizes. In my opinion, the same is true for other aspects of life where some accomplishments may seem impossible, but in reality require persistence, imagination and determination.

title: Study Abroad
text:
Villarrica, Chile | Fall 2024, 4 mos
As part of the Fall 2024 UCEAP Social-Ecological Sustainability Study Abroad Program, I researched alongside 6 other groupmembers to complete a preliminary research project on human-wildlife coexistence in Chile. The project was immensely eye-opening as we were able to learn from local farmers on how they view and coexist with predators from a local private protected area. The project used many methods including map-making, interviews and sorting categories, each of which yielded interesting results on the predators in the area and how farmers viewed them.


Group Research Project
Our group presented our research on human wildlife coexistence. Methods included a farm tour, pile sort and interview, while results included maps and analysis.

title: Study Abroad
text:
Alicante, Spain | Summer 2018, 4 wks
Summer of 2018, the Spanish Language and Culture program was my first ever study abroad program in high school. It was Spanish-language immersion, which involves speaking in Spanish 24/7. I saw huge improvements in my Spanish after just four weeks! Staying in a homestay and away from home for the first time taught me adaptability and how much the world has to offer, in addition with connecting me with my Grandma’s Spanish roots. This sparked a major interest in all things international which would eventually lead me to complete five study abroad programs, explore French language and culture, and complete a Global Studies major at UCSB.

title: Effects of Landfills on the Southern California Landscape
text:
As part of the GIS for Environmental Applications course (ENV S 154) I completed a final project which involved a group project on an environmental topic of our choosing. Our project compared two landfills in LA, the Chiquita Canyon Landfill, a landfill with various EPA violations, and the Calabasas Landfill. From the two we compared soil quality, groundwater, and environmental justice factors like income per capita. We were also able to conduct a hotspot analysis to see which data was statistically significant.
Overall, this class taught necessary GIS skills, python, as well as more advanced regression and statistical analysis. These are all skills I am looking forward to take with me as I explore the field of GIS!

text: As a recent UCSB graduate from a double major in Environmental Studies and Global Studies, I have spent a great deal of my education focused on both human and environmental interests. GIS, Statistics, and Environmentally Protected Areas give unique opportunities to explore this intersection whether through sustainable development, natural disaster mitigation, planning for sea level rise, or collaboratively managing environmentally protected areas.

title: About
text:
Origin
I credit the majority of my interest in helping the Environment to growing up in Berkeley, California. Climate Change was a constant topic of conversation and protests were the norm. It was attending so many protests that instilled in me the value of grassroots, protests, and on the ground action. While not all protests are successful, when done right with genuine passion, they can achieve great goals.
Furthermore, I was always encouraged to be open to ideas different than my own, on all sides of the political spectrum. My great-grandfather was a Supreme Court Justice who valued different perspectives. My desire to see all perspectives has also inspired an interest in protected areas, which typically involve various stakeholders with differing viewpoints, from fisherman to environmentalists.



Multicultural
While my interest in travel and the globe is mainly self-guided, my family is largely multicultural. My father is Dutch and my mother is half-Hispanic with roots tracing to the Basques of Spain. Additionally, my father grew up in Japan, thus I grew up with some Japanese influences and two older sisters who were half-Japanese. Therefore, I was always surrounded by and appreciative of other cultures.


Outside Interests
I am a big appreciator of food and the arts. I will try any food at least once and consider it a great way to build community, peer into another culture, or connect with the natural world. I also love to create art, mainly clothing. I sew many of my own clothes including my prom dress, and have volunteered at zero-waste inspired sew-repair events. Aside from fashion, there is also a lot to be learned from art history, street-art, and architecture.
